scope: Proposition 3.4 (Frame and lift torsors) of the manuscript “Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes” (preprints/Filtered-chromatic-splitting-at-generic-primes-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f2aeefc98af1afcd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The rings BU form a tower of finite étale B-algebras. After passing to normal open levels, the maps in the tower are finite étale torsors for the indicated finite deck groups. The tower is Pn-equivariant, and Pn commutes with its U0-action. Over B, the scheme of lifts of the compatible étale basis is an affine faithfully flat torsor for T = (TpΓt)m , TpΓt = lim ← − [p] Γt[pr ]. (3.6) For every r ≥ 1 its finite quotient has group T/[p]rT = Γt[pr]m and algebra B1/ptr . (3.7) Thus the full lift algebra is the algebraic root union Bperf. The group Pn acts trivially on the translation parameters. The action of (h, a) ∈ U0 on a translation tuple τ is τ 7−→ hτa−1 . (3.8) All finite torsor constructions and all their morphisms descend to finite frame levels once their finite marking data are included.
